title.rendered: APC chieftain, PDP clash over Adebutu’s emergence as Ogun gov candidate

content.rendered:
A former Acting Executive Chairman of the Federal Character Commission and chieftain of the All Progressives Congress, Kayode Oladele, has criticised the Ogun State chapter of the Peoples Democratic Party over its decision to field Oladipupo Adebutu as its governorship candidate for the 2027 election.

Oladele described the choice of Adebutu, an indigene of Iperu-Remo, the same hometown as Governor Dapo Abiodun, as politically insensitive.

In a statement issued on Sunday, the former federal lawmaker argued that it would be difficult to persuade Ogun residents to elect another indigene of Iperu immediately after the completion of Abiodun’s eight-year tenure.

He said, “Another Iperu man cannot succeed an Iperu man. Ogun people believe in fairness, equity and justice. After eight years of Governor Dapo Abiodun, who is from Iperu, no serious political party that truly understands the mood of the people would present another indigene of the same town as its governorship candidate.”

Oladele described the PDP’s decision as a political miscalculation capable of further diminishing the party’s chances in the 2027 governorship election.

He also accused the opposition party of ignoring the long-standing agitation by the people of Ogun West Senatorial District to produce the state’s governor.

According to him, Ogun West remains the only senatorial district that has not produced a democratically elected governor since the creation of Ogun State.

He said the emergence of the APC governorship candidate, Senator Solomon Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, presented an opportunity to address what he described as a long-standing political imbalance.

Oladele said, “Though Senator Adeola’s candidature is essentially about competence and popularity, it also represents an opportunity for Ogun State to correct a long-standing political imbalance.

“Ogun West has remained the only senatorial district that has not produced a governor in the history of the state. Supporting his aspiration is therefore consistent with the principles of fairness, equity and inclusive governance.”

He added that Adeola enjoyed widespread acceptance across the three senatorial districts because of his performance and empowerment programmes.

“Apart from being the most qualified and unarguably the most popular candidate in the race, Senator Adeola Yayi enjoys massive support across the three senatorial districts because of his impressive record of performance, people-oriented projects and unprecedented empowerment programmes.

“His nomination reflects both merit and the legitimate yearning of Ogun West for equitable participation in the leadership of the state,” he said.

Oladele expressed confidence that the APC would retain power in the state and urged party members to intensify grassroots mobilisation ahead of the election.

He also appealed to residents to support the second-term administration of President Bola Tinubu, saying continuity at both the federal and state levels would accelerate development.

However, the PDP dismissed Oladele’s comments, insisting that the choice of its governorship candidate was strictly an internal affair of the party.

The party’s Publicity Secretary, Kayode Adebayo, said it was not the responsibility of the APC chieftain to determine where the PDP should pick its candidate from, provided the process complied with the Constitution and the Electoral Act.

Adebayo said every political party was expected to present its strongest candidate in an election, adding that this informed the PDP’s decision to field Adebutu.

“How can a party be dictated to as regards who becomes its governorship candidate or where its candidate comes from? Candidates should emerge through a process that conforms with the party’s constitution, the national constitution and the Electoral Act as passed by the National Assembly.

“That should be what obtains in a multiparty democracy. What has the PDP done wrongly? Hon. Adebutu emerged through a process determined by the Constitution and the Electoral Act,” he said.

He urged Oladele to concentrate on the affairs of the APC instead of interfering in the PDP’s internal matters, accusing the ruling party of losing public goodwill through poor governance.

Adebayo also rejected claims that the PDP was insensitive to the aspiration of Ogun West to produce the state’s governor.

He said, “The only political party that has ever supported the aspirations of Ogun West is the PDP. In 2011, late General Adetunji Olurin was sponsored by the PDP, while in 2019, Hon. Adekunle Akinlade was supported by Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu while contesting on the platform of the APM.

“It is therefore not correct to say that the PDP has not supported the aspirations of the Ogun West people. In any election, a serious political party will present its best candidate for any office in order to serve the people through good governance. That is why Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu is being presented by the PDP for the governorship election in the 2027 general election.”
